messages:
sanjay: FYI at 05:10 UTC we're seeing NVMe IOPS bursts in ap-southeast1 that are blocking GPU attaches. attach failures spiked ~30%.
emily: any correlation with janitor/cleanup jobs or customer batch windows?
sanjay: yes - janitor started a deep-compact pass at 05:00 across scratchpool-aps1-c. IOPS metric shows sustained >85% device busy on nvme0.
tessa: host examples: gnode-aps1-112 and gnode-aps1-117. iostat: avg r/s 24k w/s 18k, await 45ms. attach queue growing.
own: can we throttle the janitor on those pools and TTR to reduce noise?
ops-bot: ALERT: nvme-io-spike.ap-southeast1 severity=warning link=https://ops.redwood/alerts/1714325000
emily: short fix: reduce janitor concurrency to 6 and mark top noisy nodes no-scrub. i'll run the patch.
tessa: also schedulers are launching a large inference batch job at 05:08; can we delay low-priority pods for 10m?
own: added a delay via placement policy for batch-job-aps1, 10m. cordoned two noisy nodes to drain GPU pods.
emily: done: kubectl -n janitor set env deploy/janitor JANITOR_CONCURRENCY=6 --overwrite; kubectl label node gnode-aps1-112 redwood/no-scrub=true
sanjay: attach backlog trending down after steps. plan: run catch-up scrubs on cold cohort overnight, add telemetry to correlate scrub windows with attach errors, and propose rate-limiter for janitor in noisy regions.
emily: agree. cost tradeoff: small extra scrub hours << customer SLA hits. will follow up with a short incident note.
ops-bot: NOTE: mitigation runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/attach-backlog
